```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = TRUE)
```

Work through this file alongside the chapter "The One-Sample t-Test" in the book. Keep it in the same folder as your `my_functions.R`.

## The data

```{r data}
scores <- c(44, 47, 48, 49, 50, 50, 51, 52, 53, 56)
comparison_value <- 49
```

## Load your toolbox

```{r load-toolbox}
library(tidyverse)
source("my_functions.R")

all.equal(my_mean(scores), mean(scores))
all.equal(my_var(scores), var(scores))
all.equal(my_sd(scores), sd(scores))
all.equal(my_se(scores), t.test(scores)$stderr)
```

You are looking for four `TRUE`s. If you see `could not find function`, finish the toolbox section at the end of the "Spread and Standard Error" exercise file first.

## Build the pieces

```{r t-pieces}
mean_score <- my_mean(scores)
se_score <- my_se(scores)

c(mean = mean_score, se = se_score)
```

### Your turn: put the pieces into the equation

Subtract the comparison value from the mean, then divide by the standard error. You should get about 0.95.

```{r t-by-hand}
t_value <-
t_value
```

### Check it against `t.test()`

```{r my-t-value-check}
t_result <- t.test(scores, mu = comparison_value)
t_result

c(mine = my_t_value(scores, comparison_value), R = unname(t_result$statistic))
all.equal(my_t_value(scores, comparison_value), unname(t_result$statistic))
```


### Check the whole test

```{r my-t-test-check}
my_result <- my_t_test(scores, comparison_value)
r_result <- tibble(
  t = unname(t_result$statistic),
  df = unname(t_result$parameter)
)

bind_rows(mine = my_result, R = r_result, .id = "version")
all.equal(my_result, r_result)
```

## A second comparison value

```{r second-comparison}
my_t_test(scores, comparison_value = 46)
t.test(scores, mu = 46)
```

Which numbers changed, and which stayed the same? Now predict the sign of t for a comparison value of 55, then check.

## Try it on real data

Did the first drug in `sleep` add any sleep, on average? If it did nothing, the mean of `extra` would be 0.

```{r real-data}
drug_1 <- sleep %>% filter(group == 1) %>% pull(extra)

my_result <- my_t_test(drug_1, comparison_value = 0)
drug_t_result <- t.test(drug_1, mu = 0)
drug_r_result <- tibble(
  t = unname(drug_t_result$statistic),
  df = unname(drug_t_result$parameter)
)

bind_rows(mine = my_result, R = drug_r_result, .id = "version")
all.equal(my_result, drug_r_result)
```

## Add to your toolbox

1. Open `my_functions.R`.
2. Copy your finished `my_t_value()` and `my_t_test()` into it, under **The One-Sample t-Test** heading. Copy only the functions.
3. Save `my_functions.R`.

Now check that the saved toolbox works on its own. You are looking for `TRUE`.

```{r toolbox-check}
rm(list = ls())
source("my_functions.R")

values <- c(44, 47, 48, 49, 50, 50, 51, 52, 53, 56)
mine <- my_t_test(values, comparison_value = 46)
theirs <- t.test(values, mu = 46)

all.equal(
  c(mine$t, mine$df),
  unname(c(theirs$statistic, theirs$parameter))
)
```

If you see `could not find function`, that function is not in `my_functions.R` yet, or the file was not saved.
